tagline: Up the Cowlitz, past the drowned towns, over to the orchards.
intro: US 12 leaves I-5 south of Napavine and heads east up the Cowlitz River to Mossyrock, between Mayfield Lake and Riffe Lake, then on through the timber town of Morton, Randle and Packwood, passing south of Mount Rainier. Twelve miles past the turn for the park's Stevens Canyon entrance it crosses White Pass at 4,500 feet. The east side comes down to Naches, where the country opens into orchards and rolling hills.
The pass was the last piece of the highway, opened in August 1951. In 1967 the road was moved ahead of Mossyrock Dam, and the lake behind it covered three towns.

moments.title: Riffe Lake
moments.text: Since the reservoir was lowered in 2017, the foundations of Kosmos show again, a logging and mercury-mining town of 500 or so emptied before the dam was finished in 1968.

moments.title: Morton
moments.text: In the 1950s it was known as the tie mill capital of the world, with the longest railroad tie dock anywhere running beside the tracks east of town.

moments.title: White Pass
moments.text: Charles White's survey party found it for the Northern Pacific in 1878. The ski area at the summit opened in 1953 and raised the racing Mahre twins.

practical: The highway is kept open all year, though the pass can close for a time in heavy winter snow.
